best_idea: Coalesce all of a frame's dirty cells into one rectangle, rebuild only that rectangle, and upload one contiguous range to the GPU instead of one upload per cell.
decision_why: Zone floor and fog layers are per-cell data that change a few cells at a time, so one range update per static layer per frame fits; port to Three.js BufferAttribute update ranges, not a line port, and split batches at the 16-bit index limit (derived, 16384 quads), not the donor's zero-quad-per-hidden-cell choice, which spends GPU time on every hidden cell.
acceptance: On a phone, opening a door repaints only the changed patch in that frame, and the GPU frame trace shows one sub-range upload per static layer per frame; a client test asserts two changes in one frame produce one flush with the merged range.
